dish.title: Nigerian Jollof Rice with Boiled Eggs
dish.description: Parboiled long-grain rice steamed in a reduced red base of blended red bell peppers, plum tomatoes, onion, and scotch bonnet with tomato paste, curry powder, thyme, bay leaves, and vegetable broth until each grain is tinted red and separate, served with halved boiled eggs.

recipe_version.title: Nigerian Jollof Rice with Boiled Eggs
recipe_version.description: Parboiled long-grain rice steamed in a reduced red base of blended red bell peppers, plum tomatoes, onion, and scotch bonnet with tomato paste, curry powder, thyme, bay leaves, and vegetable broth until each grain is tinted red and separate, served with halved boiled eggs.

ingredients.name: curry powder
ingredients.display_name: curry powder whose label lists spices only

ingredients.name: vegetable broth
ingredients.display_name: vegetable broth whose label lists vegetables, salt, and spices

steps.title: Blend the base
steps.body: Chop the bell peppers and tomatoes and cut one onion into chunks; slice the other onion thin. Blend the peppers, tomatoes, onion chunks, and scotch bonnet until smooth. Rinse the rice until the rinse runs clear.

steps.title: Reduce the base
steps.body: Heat the oil in the 5.5-quart Dutch oven over medium, about 2 minutes. Cook the sliced onion until soft, about 5 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste and cook until it darkens, about 3 minutes. Add the blended base, curry powder, thyme, bay leaves, and salt and simmer uncovered, stirring often, until reduced by about half with oil pooling at the edges, about 20 minutes.

steps.title: Boil the eggs
steps.body: While the base reduces (overlap stated): put the eggs and 6 cups water in a 3-quart saucepan and bring to a boil over high, about 8 minutes to come to a boil. Simmer 10 minutes, drain, cool under the cold tap for 3 minutes, and peel.

steps.title: Steam the rice
steps.body: Stir the rice and broth into the base and bring to a boil, about 5 minutes. Cover the pot tightly with foil and the lid, turn to low, and cook without stirring for 30 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is gone. Rest off the heat, covered, 5 minutes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Remove the bay leaves and fluff the rice with a fork. Spoon onto plates and top with the halved eggs.

scaling_notes.1: Make half the recipe (it does not reduce well smaller) in a 3-quart saucepan; boil 1 egg per serving in a 2-quart saucepan with 4 cups water.
scaling_notes.2: Half the recipe in a 3-quart saucepan; boil 2 to 3 eggs in a 2-quart saucepan with 4 cups water.
do_not_scale: the base must reduce by about half before the rice goes in, whatever the batch

coverage_contribution: Nigeria has only beef suya in the catalog, West Africa adds a red-red stew and two peanut stews, and there is no jollof or tomato-steamed rice dinner. A vegetarian, HH001-eligible one-pot rice.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with nigerian-beef-suya-skewers: a vegetarian one-pot rice, not spiced beef skewers with plain rice. Compared with spanish-chorizo-pepper-rice: steamed covered in a deep pot with a blended pepper base and eggs, not a chorizo rice. Compared with ghanaian-red-red-plantains: a tomato-pepper rice, not a black-eyed pea stew with plantains.
not_duplicate_of: Not Ghanaian jollof (no jasmine rice, no shito) and not pilau.
